title: Python SDK: Hydration proxies and idempotent streaming
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a new set of helpers in the Python SDK that provide lightweight 'hydration proxies' to convert streaming token/chunk events into typed model instances (dataclass or pydantic) in a memory and retry-safe way. This ticket covers API shape, ergonomic sync/async iterators, backpressure behavior, and clear migration guidance for existing users who parse streaming JSON manually.
acceptance_criteria: New SDK exposes HydrationProxy and AsyncHydrationProxy classes that accept either a dataclass factory or pydantic model class and a streaming chunk iterator and yield fully-hydrated model instances or partial-hydration events.

Hydration behavior is idempotent across retryable request restarts: when the runtime retries or reconnects a stream, the helper resumes without duplicating previously emitted model events (using token offsets or logical IDs).
Memory usage is bounded: proxies stream-parse JSON fragments and never buffer the full response for multi-instance outputs.
Clear examples for sync and async usage included in SDK docs and quickstart demonstrating common patterns (chat messages, batched embeddings, multi-object structured output).
Unit and integration tests cover partial hydration, out-of-order chunk fragments, and simulated reconnects/retries.
implementation_plan: Design API (this ticket): decide method names, type hints, and error model for partial vs final hydration.
Implement streaming JSON fragment parser optimized for incremental feed parsing (use python's json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode or a small C-extension later).
Create HydrationProxy sync implementation that wraps Iterable[bytes|str] -> Iterator[ModelEvent].
Create AsyncHydrationProxy for AsyncIterator sources (httpx/urllib3 async streaming).
Integrate retry metadata: accept optional stream_checkpoint callback that records last-emitted logical offset; wire into SDK retry layer to supply offset on reconnect.
Add helper converters for dataclass.from_dict and pydantic.parse_obj to be pluggable by the user.
Add tests and examples; update docs and changelog; add deprecation/migration note for users who parse raw text.
design_decisions: Expose both dataclass and pydantic pathways rather than forcing one: many users already have dataclasses and we should avoid heavy runtime dependencies.
Use a small event model (MODEL_PARTIAL, MODEL_COMPLETE, META) to represent stream lifecycle rather than trying to guarantee a single object-per-stream assumption.
Make proxies cooperative with SDK retry hooks by relying on a user-supplied checkpoint callback instead of embedding persistent storage in the helper.
Avoid implicit threading or buffering: proxies will be single-threaded and stream-driven to make behavior deterministic for backpressure-sensitive apps.
migration_notes: Existing customers who manually accumulate JSON strings and then call pydantic.parse_raw should switch to HydrationProxy to reduce latency and memory. Provide sample patterns that map old code to new helpers and note behavior differences around partial objects and error signaling.
code_samples:
# Async example with pydantic:
import asyncio
from pydantic import BaseModel

class User(BaseModel):
    id: str
    name: str

async def consume(async_stream):
    proxy = AsyncHydrationProxy(model_class=User, async_iter=async_stream)
    async for evt in proxy:
        if evt.type == 'MODEL_COMPLETE':
            user = evt.instance
            await write_user_to_db(user)

# Retry checkpoint hook example:
def checkpoint(offset_str):
    # persist last-seen offset for this customer/model in a durable store
    redis.set('stream:users:offset', offset_str)

proxy = HydrationProxy(model_class=User, stream_iter=stream_iter, checkpoint_callback=checkpoint)
testing_plan: Unit tests that feed fragmented JSON tokens (split mid-key, mid-value) and assert proper assembly into model events.
Integration test that simulates transient network failures and uses a mock checkpoint store to assert event idempotency after reconnect.
Performance microbenchmarks to measure memory allocation under large multi-object streams versus naive accumulate-and-parse approach.
Fuzz tests for invalid JSON fragments to ensure clear error events and no silent data loss.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Users will expect perfect ordering; mitigation: document ordering guarantees and provide stable logical IDs when available.
Risk: Checkpointing API may be misused leading to duplicate events; mitigation: include a recommended best-practice helper that deduplicates by stable id and timestamp.
Risk: Adding pydantic as a hard dependency increases package size; mitigation: make pydantic optional and lazy-imported, and provide explicit install extras (redwood-sdk[models]).
docs_todo: API reference for HydrationProxy / AsyncHydrationProxy with type annotations and examples.
Migration guide: manual parsing -> proxy-based streaming.
Troubleshooting: common errors when dataclass fields mismatch or when fragments are non-JSON (plain text streaming).
Notebook example (colab) showing low-latency chat UI using MODEL_PARTIAL events.
